solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dawning, as the answer to this clue will be?

parts.note: surface reading: the break of day, when the sun first shows

parts.words: as the answer to this clue will be
parts.note: setter's reading: a crossword entry is called a light, and this entry sits in the grid's opening slot, 1 Across

explanation.walkthrough: Setters call each grid entry a 'light', so the answer to 1 Across is literally the opening light of the puzzle as well as daybreak.
explanation.definitionFit: Early morning brightness, when the sun begins to rise, is the ordinary meaning of this phrase for daybreak.

clue.text: Lies first thing in flat, in bed, snoring

indicators.note: the first thing in each word is its opening letter, so only initials are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Someone lies flat out in bed, snoring away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lies' reads as lying down in bed, but it is the noun for untruths; 'first thing' reads as early morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Small untruths told casually are called fibs, a gentler plural synonym for falsehoods.

clue.text: Shout for grub

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cheer on a team or person
second meaning: to dig or rummage about, as a pig does in soil

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like a noun for food or a larva, but here it is the verb meaning to dig around.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both cheering supporters on and rummaging through earth, as pigs do when searching.

clue.text: Every Python episode? All you could desire

definitions.meaning: cryptic meaning: the whole of Monty Python, every single show
straight meaning: everything that is wanted, the lot

explanation.surface: A comedy fan wants to watch every episode of their favourite show.
explanation.walkthrough: Monty Python's Flying Circus was a British TV comedy series; the full set of its shows is jokily the complete Monty.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means everything possible or the complete works, with nothing held back or omitted.

clue.text: Old American takes lid off empty container

indicators.note: removing a lid takes away the top, which in a down entry is the first letter

parts.note: a discarded empty tin is the classic empty container

explanation.surface: An elderly American pops the lid off an empty can.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the lid is the top letter, T, so it comes off the tin can.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca empire of Peru belongs to the pre-Columbian past of South America, so its people are ancient Americans.

clue.text: Murmur ancient epic, missing last note — shame

indicators.note: missing the last means going without the final letter, so the end is lopped off

parts.note: to hum is to make a low murmuring sound
Homer's poem of the Trojan War
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone mumbles through an old epic, drops the final note, and is embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing last note' looks like one instruction, but 'missing last' trims the epic and 'note' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To shame someone is to humiliate them, making them feel degraded or foolish; both are transitive verbs.

clue.text: Round, almost colourless stone

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the letter O is round in shape
pale means lacking colour

explanation.surface: A round, nearly colourless pebble is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like an adjective for the stone, but it is the letter O by shape.
explanation.definitionFit: This milky, iridescent mineral is a well-known gemstone, often set in rings and brooches.

clue.text: Right impression promoted in irregular family group

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside its outer letters

parts.note: patchy means uneven or irregular

indicators.note: promoting something lifts it upward, and in a down entry going up means reading backwards

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
an air is an impression or appearance someone gives

explanation.surface: The right impression of a family is promoted within an unconventional household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregular' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a word for uneven that serves as the outer shell; 'promoted' works because in a down entry going up reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriarchy is a social system or family unit headed and ruled by the father or eldest male.

clue.text: Amount of light oil in musty nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook measures a little oil into some stale, musty nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' pretends to be the food being oiled; it is the word telling you to mix the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Brightness, the quantity of radiance something emits, is what this physics and everyday term measures.

clue.text: Penniless, affected by termination of loan, packed up and moved on

parts.note: broke means having no money

indicators.note: a termination is an ending, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of this word
camp means theatrically affected or exaggerated in manner

explanation.surface: A broke borrower, hit by a loan being called in, packs up and leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected by' reads as 'hit by', but 'affected' gives a piece and 'by' just places it beside the ending letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To break camp is to take down tents and leave a site; the past tense matches this verb phrase.

clue.text: Little child head sent to the back, for one thing

indicators.note: sending the head to the back moves the first letter to the end of the word

parts.note: a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A small child's head is turned away, as if in class.
explanation.walkthrough: Mite, a small child or tiny creature, moves its M to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single thing in a list or collection, one article or entry.

clue.text: Now sewn up, perhaps, painlessly?

definitions.meaning: cryptic meaning: a garment that has been mended has no rips any more
straight meaning: easily, with no crying or distress

explanation.walkthrough: The word for rips is spelt the same as the word for crying drops; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used of learning made easy, as in French for beginners with no distress or crying.

clue.text: Singlemindedness of concept for The French Connection?

definitions.meaning: straight meaning: narrow focus on one goal, ignoring all else
cryptic meaning: the original vision of the Channel Tunnel, which links Britain to France

explanation.surface: A film critic praises the single-minded idea behind the thriller The French Connection.
explanation.walkthrough: The French Connection is a 1971 film, but here it is the Channel Tunnel under the sea between England and France; a vision is a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a narrow focus on one aim, blind to everything around it, like seeing down a pipe.

clue.text: Albert, for one, look at all the mountains

parts.note: to watch is to look at
a mountain chain is a linked range of peaks

explanation.surface: Someone tells a man called Albert to gaze at the whole mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: An albert is a kind of pocket-watch chain, named after Queen Victoria's husband Prince Albert; the capital hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: The albert is a specific style of fob fastening worn across a waistcoat, so it is an example.

clue.text: Reverse fortunes? Not the record-holders

indicators.note: not means without, so these letters are removed from the phrase

parts.note: to turn the tables is to reverse a situation in your favour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sports report: the champions who held the records have seen their luck reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record-holders' suggests champions; it means the rotating platforms of a record player that hold vinyl discs.
explanation.definitionFit: Turntables are the spinning decks on which vinyl discs sit while being played, so they hold them.

clue.text: Columbine's one limb I clad in pale blue

indicators.note: to be clad in something is to be wrapped by it, so one piece is dressed in another

parts.note: aqua is a pale greenish-blue
I is the Roman numeral one
a leg is a limb
taken as written

explanation.surface: Columbine, the pantomime character, has one leg dressed in pale blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Columbine is the sweetheart of Harlequin in pantomime, but here it is the garden flower; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden flower commonly called columbine has the botanical genus name used as the answer.

clue.text: Suffer to qualify

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to endure or experience something hard
second meaning: to advance to the next round of a competition

explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffer to' reads as 'allow to', an old sense of suffer, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to endure an ordeal and to progress into the next stage of a tournament.

clue.text: God moving origin of universe back in time

indicators.note: shifting a word's starting letter later in the word changes the order of its letters

parts.note: hours are units of time

explanation.surface: A deity turns the universe back to its beginning, reversing time.
explanation.walkthrough: The U of universe, already inside HOURS, moves one place back towards the end of the word, giving the god's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Horus is the falcon-headed sky deity of ancient Egyptian religion, son of Osiris and Isis.

clue.text: Roman censor suppresses new part of poem

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down and keep in, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: Cato the Elder was a famous censor of ancient Rome
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A Roman censor bans a fresh section of a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: A censor suppressing work sounds natural; in Rome the censor was a magistrate, and Cato held that office.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto is one of the main divisions of a long poem, as in Dante's Divine Comedy.

clue.text: In brief, be returning the broken missile launcher

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters run backwards
placing one thing in another puts it inside the other's letters

parts.note: curt means brief or short
taken as written

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces that can be put back in any order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: In short, a broken missile launcher is being sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In brief' looks like the stock phrase for 'in short', but 'in' is the container signal and 'brief' is the outer word; the whole combination then turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A trebuchet is a medieval siege engine that hurled heavy stones with a counterweighted arm.

clue.text: Following plotter, do deed to acquire ship

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the second piece is placed behind the first

parts.note: a charter is someone who charts, plotting a course
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A plotter hatches a scheme to seize a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plotter' suggests a conspirator; it is one who plots positions on a chart. 'Do' is a noun for a social event.
explanation.definitionFit: In shipping law this document is the contract by which a vessel is hired from its owner.

clue.text: Sampled at intervals, hamper will do for several weeks

indicators.note: taking samples at intervals means picking every other letter

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Food sampled now and then from a picnic hamper will last several weeks.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose on purpose: a month is a run of several weeks.
explanation.definitionFit: This spring month lasts thirty days, roughly four weeks and a bit, so it is a span of weeks.

clue.text: Face losing half one's kidney treatment?

indicators.note: losing half of itself means the back half of the word is dropped

parts.note: blood filtering by machine when the kidneys fail

explanation.surface: A patient faces losing one kidney and needing treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: DIALYSIS has eight letters; dropping its last four leaves the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A dial is the face of a clock or watch, and 'dial' is also slang for a person's face.

clue.text: Lost pet has run away: wait!

indicators.note: going away means leaving, so that letter departs

parts.note: a stray is a lost or homeless animal
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An owner shouts after a lost pet that has bolted, telling it to wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay!' is also the command a dog is given, which fits the pet in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain where you are rather than leave, the same verb as wait.

clue.text: Genuinely not about to join in marriage

indicators.note: not means without, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: really means genuinely or truly
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone honestly isn't about to get married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like a time phrase, but 'about' gives RE and 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To ally is to unite families or houses by a bond, historically often by a wedding treaty.

clue.text: County celebrities ignoring unknown, bizarre artist

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Surrey is a county south of London
Y is an algebraic unknown
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: Local county celebrities snub an obscure, eccentric painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unknown' reads as an obscure artist, but it is the algebra letter taken from the county.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrealist painters such as Dali made dreamlike, strange images, so such an artist is fairly called bizarre.

clue.text: Call to abolish home counties maybe a central feature

parts.note: a cry of 'No to…' calls for something to be scrapped
the Home Counties around London lie in the south-east, SE

explanation.surface: A political campaign demands the scrapping of the home counties, a central plank.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in England's south-east; 'feature' means a part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose sits in the middle of the face, so it is one example of a central facial feature.

clue.text: Facing spread, ticked off eating large piece of cake

indicators.note: facing means sitting opposite and alongside, so two pieces stand next to each other
eating takes something inside, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold
L is the abbreviation for large
to splay is to spread out

explanation.surface: Faced with a big spread, someone scolded for gobbling a large slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of cake' looks like food at the spread, but it is the idiom for something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for a task so easy that even a youngster could manage it without effort.
